claims.statement: Lennox argues that explaining a mechanism does not exclude an agent, illustrated by Ford and the engine.
alternative_explanations: Author attribution does not establish the premise’s metaphysical truth.
limitations: Reliable attribution, not proof of a cosmic agent.

claims.statement: Lennox advances intelligibility and sophisticated laws as positive reasons for a creator and challenges naturalism’s warrant for reason.
alternative_explanations: Author attribution does not establish the premise’s metaphysical truth.
limitations: No historical or evolutionary premise independently verified here.

claims.statement: Lennox describes natural laws as regularities and denies that such laws alone rule out supernatural agency.

source_locators.locator: Paragraph beginning The laws of nature describe

alternative_explanations: Author attribution does not establish the premise’s metaphysical truth.
limitations: This is his philosophical interpretation, not a proof of miracles or the sole ontology of laws.

claims.statement: Leibniz states a PSR for true or existent facts and distinguishes necessary truths from contingent truths.
alternative_explanations: Author attribution does not establish the premise’s metaphysical truth.
limitations: Bennett modernization; universal PSR truth remains disputed.

claims.statement: Leibniz argues that even an infinite sequence of contingencies lacks its ultimate reason internally and concludes to a necessary substance.
alternative_explanations: Author attribution does not establish the premise’s metaphysical truth.
limitations: External explanation, necessity and concrete-substance steps require defense; not a temporal-beginning argument.

claims.statement: Leibniz separately attributes unity, perfection, understanding and will to the foundation, with choice governed by the best.
alternative_explanations: Author attribution does not establish the premise’s metaphysical truth.
limitations: These additional commitments are not established merely by calling a foundation necessary.

claims.statement: In Hume’s Part IX, Cleanthes objects to Demea through conceivability, a possible necessary material universe, and explanation of parts; Philo adds an analogy with hidden necessity.
alternative_explanations: Author attribution does not establish the premise’s metaphysical truth.
limitations: Speaker attribution; the conceivability premise and causal-priority conception are themselves contestable.

claims.statement: Philo challenges extrapolation from human artifacts and asks what a mental plan explains; Cleanthes replies that explaining a cause does not require explaining its cause.

source_locators.locator: Parts II,IV,V; especially Part IV pp21–23

alternative_explanations: Author attribution does not establish the premise’s metaphysical truth.
limitations: Dialogue positions; Part XII complicates a wholly negative reading. No modern cosmological result inferred.

claims.statement: Collins presents fine-tuning as comparative support over an atheistic single-universe hypothesis, explicitly short of proof or an all-things-considered verdict.
alternative_explanations: Author attribution does not establish the premise’s metaphysical truth.
limitations: Abridged original; required probability appendix absent.

claims.statement: Collins motivates life under theism through divine goodness and the value of intelligent conscious beings.
alternative_explanations: Author attribution does not establish the premise’s metaphysical truth.
limitations: Goodness and life-value are premises; cannot be counted again as independently established conclusions.

claims.statement: Collins distinguishes epistemic probability from metaphysical necessity when answering the deeper-law objection.
alternative_explanations: Author attribution does not establish the premise’s metaphysical truth.
limitations: No measure or physical parameter estimate independently established.

claims.statement: Collins answers anthropic dismissal by treating our existence as evidence and says unexplained designer complexity need not cancel comparative likelihood support.
alternative_explanations: Author attribution does not establish the premise’s metaphysical truth.
limitations: These responses do not settle selection, prior probability or the truth of likelihood premises.

claims.statement: Weisberg distinguishes old knowledge of life from newly learned stringency and questions the extra evidential contribution of stringency.
alternative_explanations: Author attribution does not establish the premise’s metaphysical truth.
limitations: Not a claim that the initial existence of life cannot favor design.

claims.statement: Weisberg derives screening-off from matched divine and blind indifference distributions, with divine intent used in his larger argument.
alternative_explanations: Author attribution does not establish the premise’s metaphysical truth.
limitations: Conditional model, not a measure-free refutation of all design hypotheses.

claims.statement: Weisberg allows initial life evidence to support design and acknowledges problems involving uniformity, unbounded spaces and parameterization.
alternative_explanations: Author attribution does not establish the premise’s metaphysical truth.
limitations: Replies by White and Bradley are mediated; later replies not independently inspected.

claims.statement: Agency compatibility does not itself favor agency; intelligibility can favor a rational creator if independently motivated comparative expectations differ.
alternative_explanations: Impersonal necessary structure; selection-and-learning proposal with empirical adequacy untested here.
limitations: Our reconstruction, not a direct quotation. No equation equates nonintentional origins with unreliable reason.

claims.statement: A restricted PSR covering contingent totality, noncircular external explanation and a concrete-ground premise conditionally yield necessary concrete reality; mentality needs further premises.
alternative_explanations: Brute totality; necessary impersonal ground; rejection of concrete-ground premise.
limitations: Our explicit reconstruction; totality contingency not inferred merely from contingent parts. Modal necessity is not temporal or causal priority.

claims.statement: Fine-tuning can supply conditional qualitative comparative support without a numerical posterior; sensitivity alone identifies neither a measure nor designer preferences.
alternative_explanations: Independently motivated deeper constraint or multiverse/selection model; matched conditional distributions.
limitations: Our comparison. Missing numerical inputs do not logically imply no evidential force. Correct Bayes identity is ours; excerpt endnote2 is malformed.

claims.statement: The inspected existence/design routes do not by themselves establish universal subjecthood, human brain independence, survival, timelessness, preservation, goodness or moral authority.
alternative_explanations: Additional independently defended premises may support stronger packages.
limitations: Our entailment assessment under T01 definitions; not a claim that no evidence for these components exists anywhere.

claims.statement: The cumulative use of these arguments must retain shared order, PSR and agent-preference dependencies rather than multiply them as independent observations.
alternative_explanations: A later dependence model could identify genuinely distinct conditional contributions.
limitations: Our method assessment. No independent empirical observations added by author agreement or repeated illustrations.

arguments.name: Mechanism and agency compatibility
premises: A mechanism explains how a process operates.
An agent explanation can concern why that process was arranged.
bridge_principles: B-T10-01: Distinct explanatory relations can coexist if their substantive causal claims do not conflict.
arguments.conclusion: A mechanism alone does not exclude agency; positive support requires an additional comparison.
arguments.strongest_objection: Observed human artifact origins do not establish cosmic agency.
arguments.strongest_reply: Unobserved causes can be inferred; require a discriminatory reason rather than direct observation as an absolute rule.

arguments.name: Intelligibility and rational origin
premises: Discoverable mathematical order is the explanandum.
A specified rational creator has independently motivated reasons to enable inquiry.
The proposed order is less expected under a defined impersonal comparison.
bridge_principles: B-T10-02: Better independently motivated expectations can supply abductive support.
arguments.conclusion: If these comparisons hold, intelligibility favors the specified rational-origin model.
arguments.strongest_objection: Agent preferences and contrast class may be fitted after observing the world; impersonal structure and learning may also explain fit.
arguments.strongest_reply: A common rational source may unify broad mathematical order and our capacity to grasp it beyond local adaptation.

arguments.name: Contingent reality and necessary concrete ground
premises: Contingent concrete totality is a legitimate contingent explanandum.
Every such contingent fact has an adequate explanation.
A complete explanation cannot be wholly internal, circular or another member of the contingent totality.
Concrete reality ultimately needs a concrete explanatory ground.
bridge_principles: B-T10-03: PSR extends to the specified contingent totality.
B-T10-04: External adequate explanation plus concrete-ground requirement excludes a wholly contingent or merely abstract ultimate basis.
arguments.conclusion: The ultimate explanatory basis includes necessary concrete reality; mind does not yet follow.
arguments.strongest_objection: Local explanations may exhaust the legitimate demand; necessary impersonal reality remains possible.
arguments.strongest_reply: Local causal links can leave why the totality obtains unanswered; exemptions from PSR need justification.

arguments.name: Fine-tuning comparative support
premises: D independently specifies an agent with reasons to produce embodied conscious life.
N specifies an impersonal alternative with less expectation of E.
Common background B and observation selection are handled consistently.
bridge_principles: B-T10-05: A larger likelihood for E under D than under N comparatively supports D; posterior odds also depend on prior odds.
arguments.conclusion: E conditionally favors D over N; this alone establishes neither an overall posterior nor the full conscious-foundation package.
arguments.strongest_objection: Sensitivity does not fix a probability measure; a designer’s choice of laws and the evidential role of life are underdetermined.
arguments.strongest_reply: Qualitative orderings can matter without exact numbers; initial life may be evidence, and unexplained cause complexity need not erase a likelihood advantage.

arguments.name: Incremental stringency and divine indifference
arguments.position: conditional objection to a class of design arguments
premises: Life O is already in background.
Design and nondesign induce the same distribution over O-compatible possibilities after conditioning.
bridge_principles: B-T10-06: Matching conditional distributions assign equal probability to the same stringency event.
arguments.conclusion: Under the matching assumptions, stringency adds no further design support once life is known.
arguments.strongest_objection: Divine and impersonal processes may justify different measures; ignorance alone is not uniformity.
arguments.strongest_reply: An argument relying on indifference must justify its asymmetric application; imposing matching distributions is an internal challenge, not an empirical law.
